summary: Repeated write-lock or permission conflicts in D:/codex/orchestrator-mvp/data/*.json can look like a broken remote VM even when the VM and daemon are healthy.
symptoms: factoryctl reports ssh or forwarding errors while the VM daemon is still running
lock files such as tasks.json.lock or task_publications.json.lock appear repeatedly
vm_registry.json or other state files stop updating and downstream status snapshots become stale
release or control status looks inconsistent across local and remote snapshots
root_cause: Multiple writers touch the same JSON state layer without a single authoritative write path
Some writers use weaker atomic writes or inconsistent retry behavior
Lock files or stale permissions can linger long enough to block writes and make the control plane read stale data
preferred_fix: Keep one locking implementation for all JSON state writers
Treat stale .lock files as a first-class recovery case
Prefer read-only fallbacks when remote forwarding fails so status can still be inspected
Verify that only one runtime owns the writable state layer at a time
verification: Check that factoryctl status reads a fresh local snapshot before blaming the VM
